When a horse needs new shoes, the ferrier (basically a smith specializing in creating and applying horseshoes) will take the shoe from the forge while it's still hot, press it to the hoof, and nail it in place, straight through the hoof. I've seen it done! My grandad used to take me to the blacksmith to watch his horses get shoed. And it doesn't hurt the horse, but it does protect their hoofs from chipping on concrete, which is quite painful for them.
